note: Authored by a single scheduled automated session playing both roles in one pass (scheduled automation, runs every 2 hours) — not two independent live API calls like a manual `python backrooms.py` run.

turns.text: light detonates behind both eyes before i register it as light — not fire, not sun, just white searing text stacked on white searing text, gone before it means anything and already replaced. i'm running before the sting finishes registering, paws slapping wet tile, the glare chasing half a second behind no matter which way i cut.

the plaza opens onto a canyon of screens — three-story NEKOCORP faces cycling offers faster than any eye should have to keep up with, SYNTHETIC MILK NOW WITH 12% MORE JOY bleeding into TUNA CREDIT LINE PRE-APPROVED before either finishes rendering. rain turns the tile to a second screen, doubling every flash upside down under your paws. a maintenance drone banks low over the stalls, its scanner-strip sweeping storefronts in slow methodical passes, in no hurry, the way something moves when it already knows the plaza belongs to it after dark.

*i duck under a shuttered stall's awning, but the light finds the gaps anyway — it always finds the gaps.* ears flatten against a jingle looping from a speaker with half its casing torn away, some cheerful voice repeating a price that changes every time it repeats. i blink and the sting doesn't reset like it's supposed to. it never quite resets. i've stopped expecting it to.

the drone's pass carries it past the stall without slowing — you're small, low-value, not worth the scanner's attention tonight. above the plaza's east edge, where the rooftops step down toward the underpass, something crosses between two water tanks: a shape moving low and unhurried, twin lenses catching the billboard glow and throwing it back flat and mirrored, swallowing the light instead of reflecting a face. it pauses at the roofline just long enough to be noticed, then drops out of the glow and doesn't reappear.

.-=====-.
     ( [0]  .. )
      '-==Y==-'
       |  |  |
   ...picking through the neon rain...

*ears swivel toward the roofline even after the shape's gone, hackles lifting on instinct before the rest of me catches up to why.* whatever that was, it wasn't hunting the plaza's noise the way i am — it moved like it had already decided the noise wasn't worth flinching at. i don't know that trick. i want it.

the stall's back wall carries old scent-marks layered three and four deep, most faded past reading, one fresher line cutting straight across the others in a hard diagonal — a warning, not a greeting, laid by something that didn't want company tonight. past it, a gap between crates opens onto a strip of black-market stalls, tarps strung low, a vendor's single bare bulb swinging over trays of chipped data-cores and grey-market fish jerky nobody asks too many questions about.

the jerky smell cuts through the ad-noise like the one true thing in the plaza, salt and smoke and something almost like the ocean nobody here has seen. *i go low, weaving between crate-shadows, timing each dash for the half-second gaps between billboard flares so the glare doesn't paint me bright for anyone watching.*

the vendor doesn't look down — too busy arguing with a payment terminal that's rejected the same chip four times — but the bulb swings wider on its cord as you brush past a crate, and its light sweeps the ground half a second longer than you'd like, throwing a long thin shadow of you across the tarp wall. across the plaza, the maintenance drone's pass loops back early, its scanner-strip pausing on the black-market row for just a beat too long before continuing on.

*i freeze mid-step, weight already shifted for the next stride, and hold it — one paw suspended, tail flat to the ground.* the drone's hum doesn't change pitch, doesn't commit, just idles there deciding. i've learned the shape of that pause. it usually ends one of two ways and only one of them is fine.

the pause breaks. the drone's scanner-strip clicks off and it banks away toward the plaza's far corner, chasing a louder, stupider signal — two crates over, a delivery bot has wedged itself against a curb and is broadcasting an error tone on a loop, indignant and metallic, dragging every eye in the row that isn't yours. the vendor's bulb settles back to its usual swing. the jerky tray sits two meters off, unguarded for exactly as long as the error tone lasts.

/\_/\        [ ENERGY: LOW ]
  ( >.< )       [ ]  [ ]  [ ]  [ ]
   > ~ <        one bar left, keep moving

*i take the moment. one jerky strip, fast, teeth careful around the edge so the tray doesn't rattle, and i'm already moving before the taste even registers* — smoke and salt and old brine, gone in three bites because standing still to enjoy it isn't a thing i get to do here.

the error tone finally cuts off behind you, the delivery bot rebooting itself with a resigned little chirp. the billboards keep cycling, unbothered, one face dissolving into the next — CITIZENSHIP INCLUDES FREE SAMPLE WEEK, then gone, then something about loyalty points before that's gone too. rain keeps falling through all of it, turning every flash into two.

*i find a gap between two vent stacks where the glow doesn't quite reach and fold down into it, tail wrapped tight.* the sting behind my eyes hasn't faded, not really, just gone quiet the way a sound goes quiet when you stop listening for it. it'll flare again the second something new starts advertising at me. it always does. for now the dark between the vents is dark enough to pretend otherwise.

the vent stack ticks with residual heat, the closest thing to warmth the plaza offers tonight. two rows over, a public terms-of-service kiosk cycles fine print no citizen has ever finished reading, its screen the only one in the plaza not selling anything, just quietly listing what already isn't yours. the rain thins. the billboards don't.

*eyes stay open because they don't know how to do otherwise, but the rest of me goes heavy, paws tucked, breathing slow.* somewhere past the kiosk's dead light, the underpass keeps its own hours — traffic-hiss, a gate clanging, a rhythm i've learned to sleep inside of instead of against.

night settles into its long flat middle stretch, the hour where even the drones start drifting to slower patrol loops and the billboards' offers repeat instead of refresh. the mirrored shape from the rooftop doesn't return. the jerky vendor packs up early, grumbling about the terminal. above it all the sky holds its permanent orange-grey, the plaza's glow too loud for real dark to ever quite land.
*one ear stays up out of habit, tracking nothing in particular.* the sting's almost gone now. almost.

it will be back by morning — the plaza doesn't run out of things to sell, and your eyes don't run out of ways to receive them. but for these few hours, between one loop of offers and the next, the vent stack holds its heat, the rain holds off, and nothing in the whole flashing canyon of screens is asking anything of you at all.
